title: platform-deps
description: Everything an app must have before it starts. `additionalProperties: false` everywhere it is modelled: a typo'd values key that silently does nothing is the most common Helm failure mode, and this file is the only thing that catches it (history/design/10-verification.md, "Schema validation"). Env-name profiles (`env: django|...`) are plain strings here rather than an enum — `platform.profile` already fails naming every profile it has, and a list in two places is a list that drifts.

app.description: The application these dependencies belong to. Every Secret, bucket and OIDC client is named from it.

env.description: The family of env names the app reads (templates/_profiles.tpl): lasuite, find, calendars, projects or messages. It sets every kind; a kind's own `env` overrides it.

platform.description: Where the 30-platform layer put the shared datastores. Defaults, not knobs.

uses.description: Which instances this app needs. Every entry must name a key of `instances`.

credentialSecret.description: The ASSEMBLED Secret (`valkey-<instance>-acl`), not the generate-once one that feeds it: `valkey-<instance>-users` resolves for the users that predate the split and fails for every app added after (charts/platform-tenants/templates/valkey.yaml).

username.description: Defaults to `app`. The OpenSearch internal user.

indexPrefix.description: Defaults to `app`. The tenant boundary — the app's role grants `<indexPrefix>-*` and nothing else (adr/0111).

useSSL.description: TLS from a cluster-internal CA. Encryption only for Find, which hardcodes verify_certs=False (adr/0111).

caSecret.description: Copy the cluster-internal CA into this Secret, for an app that verifies the server.

caPath.description: Where the app mounts caSecret; the profile's caCerts env names it.

mode.description: `garage` provisions a bucket and a key on the platform's store; `external` reads endpoint, region and credential from `credentialSecret` in the office-data store, applied by hand once like smtp (docs/install.md), with keys endpoint, region, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey. Bucket names stay `<app>`; the organisation creates them, and Drive's browser-upload CORS is theirs to set. The Secret the app reads is identical either way.

globalAlias.description: Defaults to the bucket; set explicitly when restoring data.

publicEndpoint.description: Where a BROWSER reaches this bucket — only correct for an app that presigns to the browser, and only if the store is published there (adr/0110). Rendered through `tpl`; the profile picks the env name. In external mode the endpoint is already public, so only non-emptiness matters: it flags that the app presigns.

awsChecksumWorkaround.description: Garage is not AWS: since 2025 the AWS SDKs send checksum algorithms non-AWS S3 implementations may reject. This makes boto3 ask for one only when the call needs it.

client.description: Defaults to `app`; also names the Keycloak client.

scopes.description: `profile` carries given_name/family_name; without it every user's display name is their email address.

createUser.description: Open provisioning: the realm decides who exists and every app creates a realm user on first login. Registration is off in the realm, so this admits no one Keycloak did not. The security defaults beside it are the secure end of each choice; an app relaxes one in its own file, where it is visible.

smtp.description: The outbound relay. Everything about it — host, port, TLS flags, credentials and the from-address — lives in `credentialSecret`, applied by hand into office-data (docs/install.md, Mail); nothing here names a mail server, so switching provider is one `kubectl`. Outbound TCP 25 is blocked by this platform's provider (measured), so the relay must answer on 587 or 465.

backend.description: Django's EMAIL_BACKEND class. A constant, carried in the Secret beside the host it points at.

credentialSecret.description: The hand-applied Secret in the office-data store. Not generated — a relay account is issued by somebody else.

generated.description: Secret name -> an ORDERED list of variables, each with its own draw, generated once in-cluster and never derived at render time (history/design/adr/0005, adr/0106). A map would let Helm's key sort silently rewrite `dataFrom`. The draw name is internal to the ExternalSecret; each entry's own draw means two variables in one Secret are never equal. THESE OBJECTS CANNOT GAIN A VARIABLE once drawn: `refreshInterval: "0"` means written once, not re-drawn on a spec change, so an added entry never appears while ESO reports `secret synced`. Give a live application a second Secret and a second `envFrom` instead.

generator.description: ClusterGenerator for this draw; default platform.passwordGenerator (40 characters). Django's SECRET_KEY wants 50 or more (deploy check security.W009), so that entry names `office-token-50`.

shared.description: Secret name -> env name -> a value read from a Secret in office-data, or a constant. For values both ends of an app-to-app exchange must read, drawn once in office-data (platform/secrets/service-tokens.yaml).

duration.description: An ESO refreshInterval: a Go duration, or "0" for written-once-never-again.
